prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts an open agricultural field receding smoothly from bright foreground objects within arm's reach (0.3–0.8 m)—specifically the camera wearer's hands, a mobile phone, a blue bucket with a yellow container inside at the bottom center, and a transverse black irrigation pipe on the ground about 1.2–1.5 m ahead—to a dark horizon and treeline over 20 m away. In frame 1, the camera looks down at the buckets with a person's legs partly out of view at the top right (~3.5 m away), while across frames 2–5 the camera tilts up to show that person seated on a white chair in a furrow 4–6 m ahead (shifting from center-right to center-left) facing and looking toward the camera wearer with a phone at his ear. A second standing person enters at the far right edge in frame 3 (~4 m away, partly out of view and ~2 m right of the seated man) and approaches across frames 4–5 to stand ~2–2.5 m ahead on the right, facing and looking down toward the camera wearer while the wearer's right hand extends the phone to ~0.5 m in front of the chest, partially occluding the standing man's lower right leg and the blue bucket below. The depth map makes the continuous ground-plane gradient, the elevated ridge of the foreground irrigation pipe, and the step-by-step closing distance between the approaching standing man and the seated man much clearer than in the RGB image alone. However, the map is unreliable on distant background details—completely losing a third crouching person on the far left of the crop field (~15–20 m away in frames 1–2)—and flattens the seated person's chair legs and the standing man's feet into the surrounding soil.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates foreground and mid-ground people and handheld objects against an unlabelled black background where the field, irrigation pipes, chair, and buckets are omitted. At the bottom within arm's reach (0.3–0.6 m), masks track the camera wearer's left and right hands and forearms holding and then extending a cell phone in frames 2–5 (which partly occludes the blue bucket below and the standing man's lower leg in frame 5), while in the mid-ground a seated person facing the camera wearer is segmented 4–6 m ahead in frames 2–5 alongside a second standing person who enters partly out of view on the right edge in frame 3 (~4 m away) and approaches to ~2–2.5 m ahead on the right by frame 5, about 2–3 m closer to the wearer than the seated man. The map highlights the exact pixel boundaries of the cell phone in frames 3–5, the separation between the wearer's two hands, and the tiny silhouette of the distant crouching person ~15–20 m to the left in frame 2, which blends into the green crops in the RGB image. However, it is highly unreliable in class labels and completeness: it misclassifies the distant person on the left as a 'cow', labels the seated man's torso as a 'backpack' and the foreground phone and bucket rim as 'skateboard' in frame 2, labels the wearer's hands and arms as separate 'person' instances, and completely misses the foreground buckets, the white chair, the seated man's legs in frame 1, and his handheld phone.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank black across all five frames, failing to render body or hand skeletons for nearly all people in the scene despite clear RGB visibility of the camera wearer's hands in the bottom foreground (0.3–0.6 m away), the seated man facing the camera 4–6 m ahead in the center furrow, the standing man approaching on the right from ~4 m to ~2–2.5 m in frames 3–5, and the distant crouching person ~15–20 m to the left in frames 1–2. In frame 1, only a single isolated yellow body keypoint dot appears near the bottom-left on the camera wearer's left hand (~0.3 m away, beside the occluded blue and yellow buckets), and in frame 2, a compact cluster of magenta hand keypoints localizes the fingers of the wearer's left hand gripping the top of the black phone ~0.4 m in front of the viewer. This magenta cluster in frame 2 pinpoints the fine finger articulation and grip orientation on the dark phone body against the dark soil, which is somewhat harder to separate at a glance in the RGB strip. Overall, however, the pose map is severely unreliable: it misses the wearer's hands completely in frames 3–5 as the right arm reaches forward toward the approaching man, and it provides zero skeletal data to determine the posture, facing direction, gaze toward the camera wearer, or relative 3D arrangement of the mid-ground and background people.
